requirements.text: The ACPE ESA sample(s) submitted for type approval shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3. shall be affixed to every ACPE ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10.

The vehicle and its ACPE electrical/electronic system(s) or ESA(s) shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be tested for radiated emissions for vehicle type approval.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances for vehicle type approval.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for radiated emissions.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for conducted emissions.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances.
The ACPE ESA(s) shall be tested for immunity to conducted disturbances.

Where broadband radiation is measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 32 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where broadband radiation is measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 32 to 43 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz.

Where broadband radiation is measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band.

Where broadband radiation is measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 3.

Where broadband radiation is measured using the method described in Annex 4 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle broadband emission limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured broadband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband radiation limit shall be 28 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 10.0 ± 0.2 m, the vehicle narrowband radiation limit shall be 35 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband radiation limit shall be 38 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 230 MHz frequency band.

Where narrowband measurements are made using the method described in Annex 5 with a vehicle-to-antenna spacing of 3.0 ± 0.05 m, the vehicle narrowband radiation limit shall be 45 dB microvolts/m in the 230 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the vehicle representative of its type, the measured narrowband electromagnetic radiation values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limit.

Where immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle shall withstand a field strength of 30 volts/m in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

Where immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-2, the vehicle shall withstand a field strength of a minimum of 25 volts/m over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

Where immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the vehicle shall withstand a current of 60 mA in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

Where immunity tests are made using the method described in Annex 6 in accordance with ISO 11451-4 BCI, the vehicle shall withstand a current of a minimum of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 2,000 MHz frequency band.

During the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 6, the vehicle representative of its type, including the ACPE system, shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions", according to paragraph 2.1. of Annex 6.

The broadband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 7, shall be 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

The broadband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 7, shall be 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
The broadband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 7, shall remain constant at 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The broadband emission values measured on the ACPE ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The narrowband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

The narrowband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz frequency band, increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
The narrowband type approval limit for the ACPE ESA, where measured using the method described in Annex 8, shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
The narrowband emission value measured on the ACPE ESA representative of its type, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines by the ACPE ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For the stripline method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the TEM cell method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the BCI method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the ALSE method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band.
For the stripline method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a minimum test level of 50 V/m over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
For the TEM cell method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m over the whole 20 to 200 MHz frequency range.
For the BCI method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a minimum test level of 50 mA over the whole 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

For the ALSE method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a minimum test level of 25 V/m over the whole 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 8 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.

For the reverberation chamber method, the ACPE ESA shall meet the immunity requirements at a minimum test level of 18 V/m over the whole LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 6 V/m over the whole 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ACPE ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

For ACPE variants that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V starter motor, the ACPE ESA shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses, with functional status classification B for immunity related functions if the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, as defined in ISO 16750-1.

For ACPE variants that could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V starter motor, the ACPE ESA shall withstand the starting profile at immunity test level II with 10 pulses, with functional status classification C for immunity related functions if the ESA need not be operational during engine start phases, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 1 at -75 V on a 12 V system for 500 pulses with FPSC III as in ISO 7637-1.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 2a at +37 V on a 12 V system for 500 pulses with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 2b at +10 V on a 12 V system for 10 pulses with FPSC II for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 3a at -112 V on a 12 V system for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The ACPE ESA shall withstand test pulse 3b at +75 V on a 12 V system for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and FPSC III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m and measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 28 dBµV/m in the frequency range 30-230 MHz.
The vehicle narrowband radiated emissions, at an antenna-vehicle separation of 10 m and measured with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed E = 35 dBµV/m in the frequency range 230-1,000 MHz.
The vehicle electronic systems shall meet the immunity requirements at the test levels defined in paragraph 6.4.2.1. of this Regulation.
In the "50 km/h mode" immunity test, the instrument cluster shall operate in normal mode without unexpected warning.
The vehicle shall not set itself in motion during the immunity test in REESS charging mode.
The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall meet the immunity requirements when exposed to electromagnetic radiation in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges in vertical polarization.

The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall meet the immunity requirements when exposed to AM (amplitude modulation) test signals with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.

The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall meet the immunity requirements when exposed to PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signals, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.

The vehicle fitted with the ACPE system shall meet the immunity requirements when exposed to PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signals, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
The ACPE electronic sub-assembly shall meet the narrowband emission limits of Annex 8 throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with AM (amplitude modulation) test signal modulation, with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signal modulation, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements with PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signal modulation, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges.
The ACPE ESA shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply, as tested according to Annex 10.
The ACPE ESA shall limit the conducted transients it emits to the vehicle power supply, as tested according to Annex 10.

Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under UN R175 shall bear an international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2, affixed conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form.

Where the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under UN R175 and the circle symbol is not repeated, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.
The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be forward.

The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle when the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.

The ACPE shall regard as an accelerator control misapplication an accelerator control application having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of the accelerator control of at least 90 per cent with that velocity.
The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill.
If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 seconds after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver.
The information that the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention shall exist until the system has been successfully initialised.

The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located between 1.0 m and 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the accelerator control is applied, provided the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion and the weather conditions do not affect the performance of the vehicle (e.g. no storm, not below 0°C).

When conditions deviate from those specified for the ACPE performance requirement, the ACPE shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy, as demonstrated in accordance with Annex 3.

In the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the ACPE triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2. are met.

In the case that a collision is not prevented, the collision speed shall not be greater than 70% of that speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances but without any ACPE intervention.

For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the ACPE speed reduction shall be of at least 15 per cent.
During any ACPE intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE until the obstacle is no longer detected or the driver has interrupted the function.

The effectiveness of the ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields, as demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
The ACPE shall meet the requirements of Annex 3 concerning the safety aspects of electronic control systems.
The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
The interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
In the case of interruption of the ACPE intervention by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.

Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant), except when the new engine start (or run cycle) is performed automatically, e.g. by the operation of a stop/start system.
Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.
A failure warning shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of UN R175 being met.
There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check.

In the case of an electrically detectable ACPE failure, there shall not be a delay in illuminating the warning signal, except that if the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time the failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.

A failure warning shall be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical ACPE failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment), unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
The ACPE optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
The satisfactory condition of the ACPE optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.

Each ACPE optical warning signal not shown in a common space shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is in a position between the "on" (run) and "start" position that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system (power-on)).
The ACPE intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal.

The ACPE shall provide a haptic or acoustic signal to the driver in addition to the optical intervention warning signal, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
The ACPE failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
It shall be possible at a Periodic Technical Inspection to confirm the correct operational status of the ACPE by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.

Following a "power-ON" and any bulb check, the ACPE failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.

The ACPE shall have means to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal, unless a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE is available.
The ACPE shall intervene in the forward direction with the target present at a distance of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the requirements without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivation in the forward direction at a distance to the speed measuring point of 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) without a target.
The ACPE shall intervene in the rearward direction with the target present at a distance of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) and a lateral offset tolerance of +/-0.2 m.

The ACPE shall meet the requirements without ACPE intervention or with ACPE deactivation in the rearward direction at a distance to the speed measuring point of 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) without a target.
The ACPE system shall be designed to operate, under non-fault and fault conditions, in such a way that it does not induce safety critical risks.
The ACPE system shall respect, under non-fault and fault conditions, all the appropriate performance requirements specified elsewhere in UN R175.

Each unit of the ACPE system shall be clearly and unambiguously identifiable (e.g. by marking for hardware and marking or software output for software content) to provide corresponding hardware and documentation association.

Where ACPE functions are combined within a single unit or within a single computer but shown in multiple blocks in the block diagram, only a single hardware identification marking shall be used for that unit.
The identification of an ACPE system unit shall define the hardware and software version.
The identification of an ACPE system unit shall be changed where the software changes such as to alter the function of the unit as far as UN R175 is concerned.
In case of a failure of the ACPE system, the driver shall be warned, for example by warning signal or message display.

Where the ACPE system is not deactivated by the driver (e.g. by turning the ignition (run) switch to "off" or by switching off the function with a special switch), the failure warning shall be present as long as the fault condition persists.
Where the chosen fault provision is the removal of the ACPE function, all output control signals associated with the ACPE function shall be inhibited.
Where the chosen fault provision is the removal of the ACPE function, the output control signals shall be inhibited in such a manner as to limit the transition disturbance.

The ACPE system shall not prejudice the safe operation of the vehicle when its performance is affected by environmental conditions such as climatic conditions, temperature, dust ingress, water ingress or ice packing.
The ACPE system shall perform the functions declared by the manufacturer under non-fault conditions, including scenarios whereby a declared function is overridden.

The reaction of the ACPE system to a failure in any individual unit, simulated by applying corresponding output signals to electrical units or mechanical elements, shall be in accordance with the manufacturer's declared safety concept, including vehicle controllability and user information (HMI) aspects.

The reaction of the ACPE system under the influence of a failure in any individual unit shall correspond with the documented summary of the failure analysis, to a level of overall effect such that the safety concept and execution are confirmed as being adequate.
